definition: Describes moments that participants acknowledged a meaningful influence of gender in the context of food.
example: Do you think women sometimes find the idea of eating less meat or no meat more palatable than men do? I only say that because I live with five women and um, sort of a lot, most of them would happily not eat meat at all. Um, and also partners of quite a lot of my friends don't eat a lot of meat and wouldn't, they would, they would happily eat no meat at all. Whereas all of us, we, you know, we like our meat.
quote:
I think there's something about being a man and meat, isn't there? Like, you grow up with a certain idea of what a proper meal is — and that's meat. Red meat especially. Steak, a chop, a bit of mince. That's what fills you up, that's what a real dinner looks like. And that sticks with you.

And then there's the other side of it — the pub, the lads, all of that. You're not sitting there discussing what you're eating or thinking about nutrition or any of that. You just order what you always order. You don't question it. There's an assumption, I think, that men just eat meat and don't fuss about it. And you sort of... go along with that without really noticing.

definition: Describes moments that participants reported no possible association between gender and food.
example: I don't think gender influences what I eat at all. Um, like if there's something I want I'll just have it. There's no such thing as a manly or womanly dish if you ask me, it's just like, it's just food. And like, so it's literally got zero influence on whether I'd eat something or not.

definition: Describes moments that participants rejected or were unsure of the idea of a gender influence, but went on to discuss highly gendered food contexts (e.g. barbecuing, portion sizes, who does the cooking) seemingly without awareness, or recognition of the gendered nature of these comments.
example: Um, I don't think gender influences what I eat. Maybe how much I eat with my like guy friends compared to my girls that are friends. But I don't like, where we go to, not really. It's usually just all the same. I might order a bit more, but that's not really relevant.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed the “naturalness” of animal products (e.g. familiar ingredients, lack of preservatives or additives).
example: So like chicken will just say chicken on the back. Whereas a plant based one would have something like glycolic acid or something. I have no idea what that is.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed eating animal products as socially normative or default.
example: Yeah, that's right. It's what what you, what what was put on the table. You were told to eat. Yeah. And I know that I, I remember very vividly that every Sunday. It was Sunday roast and Monday was cold meat and, you know, and so it went on. Um, so it's, yeah, everybody, I think, was brought up virtually the same, depending on the family circumstances.
quote: And yeah, technically I could say let's have fish instead of the roast. But there's an assumption, isn't there? Sunday roast means meat. Proper meat. My wife would think I was being odd about it. Not that she'd say no — she wouldn't — but there's this... pressure, almost, to just do things the way they've always been done. Because that's what normal is out here.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed animal products as a necessity, usually due to health/fitness concerns (e.g. protein intake), among others (e.g. supporting local farmers).
example: Protein, you're building up the, perhaps if you're going to the gym, you're building up muscles, strength, et cetera. Yeah, exactly. Meat obviously helps.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed how tasty or enjoyable animal products are.
example: Um, yeah, I've thought quite often over the years of whether I could go, um, vegetarian or, vegan I definitely couldn't do. I like dairy too much. But, um, I, I would struggle to go completely plant based just cause I like, I like meat too much. Um, I could definitely restrict, reduce my meat intake... but then I would start craving some chicken or, or, or steak or something like that. Um, no, I would. Just enjoyment for me of food, I wouldn't, I wouldn't get so much from eating.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed the “unnaturalness” of plant-based products (e.g. unfamiliar ingredients or processing, presence of preservatives or additives).
example: But then you know, if you think about stuff like plant based cheese, it's like how on earth did you even make that? Like, I don't know I don't understand the processes of manufacturing like to the finer details but do you take the plant and turn it into cheese? Like surely that must be processed in some really odd way.
quote: And the names matter too. Don't call it a meat substitute. That's admitting it's not as good. Just call it what it is — a lentil stew, a bean chilli. Men will eat it if it's good and it fills you up. They won't eat it if it feels like you're doing it for the right reasons.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed plant-based products being unable to meet nutritional needs.
example: Yeah, I'd struggle to get all my protein... Um, I know that someone, a vegan would probably say, oh, yeah, I can get everything from this particular dish and that food, but I sometimes struggle to get my head around whether it would, you do get everything you need without supplements and all that kind of stuff.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed the unpleasant taste or texture of plant-based products.
example: It's just a bit bland, innit, sometimes? It just doesn't taste right.

definition: Describes moments that participants discussed the extreme circumstances that would have to occur for them to adopt a fully plant-based diet.
example: But, um, really, I think this, the, the, the catalyst for that for me would be, um, it would only really be health related stuff. If someone said to me you’re gonna have to do this, or it's going to knock years off your life.
